svg.title: Глава 7 — Прикладной уровень: итоговая шпаргалка
svg.desc: Вся глава: DNS → mail → Web/HTTP/privacy → multimedia → CDN/P2P
svg.text: Вся глава: DNS → mail → Web/HTTP/privacy → multimedia → CDN/P2P

text.tspan: Hierarchical naming + distributed database.
Resolver follows delegation toward authoritative server.
Resource records carry addresses, NS/MX/aliases/services.
Caching + TTL improve performance and resilience.
Plain DNS exposes queried names to network observers.
DoT/DoH encrypt resolver traffic on part of the path.
Resolver centralization changes who can observe queries.
dig provides a source-supported way to inspect resolution.
User agents create/read messages; transfer agents relay them.
SMTP/ESMTP transfers mail; DNS MX selects receiving server.
MIME extends message format beyond basic text.
IMAP supports remote mailbox access; webmail uses Web UI.
URL names resource/scheme/host/path.
HTTP is request-response; HTTPS adds protected transport.
Methods + status codes define operation/result.
Persistent connections and caching reduce overhead.
HTTP/3 is discussed as a newer HTTP form using UDP context.
Server-side code can generate content from application/data.
Client-side scripts make browser pages interactive.
Cookies preserve state across nominally stateless requests.
Third-party tracking, cookie syncing and fingerprinting
can correlate activity across sites/devices.
Digital media requires encoding/compression.
Delay matters for interactive media; jitter affects playback.
Playback buffer converts irregular arrival into smoother output.
DASH/HLS use short alternative representations for adaptation.
Stored streaming and real-time communication have different needs.
RTP/RTCP context carries media timing/feedback.
H.323 combines multiple protocols for multimedia calls.
SIP provides modular signaling and user location/redirect flow.
Signaling and media transport are separate responsibilities.
Browser cache is first local reuse layer.
Web proxy offers shared cache for many users.
Server farms scale origin capacity.
CDN distributes caches and selects nearby delivery nodes.
DNS can participate in mapping users to content copies.
Peers act as both clients and content suppliers.
Torrent metadata describes chunks and tracker information.
Tracker/DHT helps discover peers.
Rare-piece selection improves replication.
Choking/incentives discourage free-riding.

svg.text: Provenance: RAG p0685:c01–p0813:c01 · detailed visual covers sections 7.1–7.6
